reuse.why: The tree already has the shared getScheduledAmount helper (used by the client and meant for exactly this), yet every changed site re-implements the range/approximate rule inline and the helper itself is left on the old midpoint rule.

duplication.why: The 'endpoint furthest from zero' ternary is written three times (api-models, schedule-template, forecast-schedules) and a fourth, different variant in the preview code.

placement.why: A rule about schedule amounts belongs in shared/schedules (getScheduledAmount); instead it is scattered into the API model, the budget template and the forecast normalizer.

scope.why: Edits stay on schedule-amount sites, but the end state is half-applied: only the preview gets the step-3/4 rules while schedules/app.ts posting and updateActions are untouched.

maintainability.why: Four inline copies now disagree (preview uses lowest/approx-tolerance, the others furthest-from-zero, posting still uses the midpoint), so each future rule change must hunt every copy.

bypasses_abstraction.where: api-models.ts scheduleModel.toExternal, budget/schedule-template.ts createScheduleList, forecast/forecast-schedules.ts normalizeSchedule and shared/schedules.ts computeSchedulePreviewTransactions inline the rule instead of updating and calling getScheduledAmount

disguised_duplication.where: The preview copy reshapes the same endpoint selection as num1 <= num2 ? num1 : num2 and adds -getApproxNumberThreshold inline, a reworded variant of the furthest-from-zero ternaries elsewhere

abstraction_drift.where: getScheduledAmount in shared/schedules.ts is never updated; api-models toExternal, schedule-template createScheduleList, forecast normalizeSchedule and computeSchedulePreviewTransactions each carry their own inline copy
